text.p: Mexican builder ICA plans to bid for Panama's privatizations of water distribution, electricity generation and airports, the company's president said on Thursday.
"We will participate in water, electricity, airport, garbage, all infrastructure," ICA's Bernardo Quintana told reporters.
Quintana said the company will look for a local partner for the privatizations, which were presented in this central Mexican town by Panama's president Ernesto Perez Balladares.
ICA's president said the company would talk with an unnamed French company with which they have worked in the past in water projects.
Quintana added that in the next 18 months the company would invest about $220 million in the construction of an urban expressway from the airport to the center of Panama.
The president of the Latin American nation said the water aqueduct to be tendered in coming months will distribute drinkable water through the country.

Panama also plans to privatize its thermoelectric plants in five segments, and privatize its three airports, Perez said. The government said electicity output grew 5.5 percent in 1996 to 1.012 million kilowatts per hour.
The privatizations will be ready in the next year, with the airport tender ready before year end, Ricardo Duran, director of the commission to promote investment in Panama, said.
